# novu_layout (Resource)

Layout resource. Manage an email layout within the environment.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "novu_layout" "example" {
  layout_id = "example-layout"
  name      = "Example layout"
  email = {
    body = <<-EOT
      <html>
        <body>
          {{content}}
        </body>
      </html>
    EOT
  }
}

resource "novu_workflow" "example" {
  workflow_id = "example-workflow-id"
  name        = "example workflow"
  steps = [
    {
      email_step = {
        name = "email step"
        control_values = {
          subject   = "example subject"
          body      = "<p>example body</p>"
          layout_id = novu_layout.example.layout_id
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `email` (Attributes) Email content of the layout (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--email))
- `layout_id` (String) Unique identifier of the layout, used by email steps to reference it
- `name` (String) Name of the layout

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Database identifier of the layout
- `is_default` (Boolean) Whether the layout is the default layout of the environment

<a id="nestedatt--email"></a>
### Nested Schema for `email`

Required:

- `body` (String) Body of the layout. Must contain the `{{content}}` variable where the email step content is rendered, and for the `html` editor a full document with `<html>` and `<body>` tags.

Optional:

- `editor_type` (String) Type of editor used for the body. Allowed values: `block`, `html`. Defaults to `html`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a layout by its layout_id
terraform import novu_layout.example <layout_id>
```
